prior_importants.description: In a remeasure, `config` is a fresh checkout of `targetSha`, which never holds a gitignored `.pnp.cjs`, so the new Plug'n'Play branch never fires there and the refusal still tells the operator to run `yarn --cwd . install`, which the PR says can never clear it.

findings.description: `isPackageName` still accepts `.bin`, `.pnpm` and a bare scope such as `@types`. All three always exist under an installed `node_modules`, so a manifest that declares one skips the refusal. To close it, require exactly two segments for a scoped name and reject any segment that starts with `.`.

The ADR 0081 amendment heading says the Plug'n'Play runtime "is trusted only from the main checkout". In a remeasure the code trusts it from the stand-in (`config`), and the main checkout's runtime never skips the refusal. "from the config checkout" would match the code.
The new ADR 0081 amendment is dated but cites only #330, not this PR. docs/adr/README.md §Reading and writing asks for an amendment "dated, with the PR", so it should name #380.

process_issues.description: Kept one correctness and one security instance, as in round 1: about 140 of the diff's lines are a byte-identical move. Skipped context (no infra or protocol surface), maintainability (off the default roster), spec (no closing issue) and workflow-safety (no workflow change). Dropped a docs nit about the 'the target' wording in the Plug'n'Play error: its reviewer said the wording is correct wherever it is reachable.
